summary:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday that a security breach affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially the biggest crypto heist on record. The company said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, and it halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. Experts have identified North Korea as the likely culprit, and cryptocurrency prices fell on the news.

A train crash near Toledo, Spain, has killed at least 69 people, one of the deadliest in the country's history. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said people of 27 nationalities may be among those killed or injured, and at least 70 people are reported missing. The death toll may rise further. Transport Minister Óscar Puente was expected to give an update.

Israel's final election results confirm that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority of parliamentary seats, though it finished ahead of the opposition. Arab parties won one in six seats and could become kingmakers, and Likud alleged, without providing evidence, that their gains were driven in part by voter fraud. Weeks of difficult coalition talks lie ahead, and the results could lead to another vote.

headlines.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
headlines.summary: Binance said a security breach affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially the largest crypto heist on record. The company has recovered or frozen about $3 billion, and experts have identified North Korea as the likely culprit.

headlines.title: Train crash near Toledo, Spain, kills at least 69 people
headlines.summary: The crash near Toledo has killed at least 69 people and at least 70 are reported missing, making it one of the deadliest in the country's history. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said people of 27 nationalities may be among those killed or injured.

headlines.title: Netanyahu's bloc loses majority in final Israeli election results
headlines.summary: Final results show Netanyahu's bloc finished ahead but short of a majority, while Arab parties won one in six seats. Likud alleged without evidence that Arab parties' gains were partly driven by voter fraud, and coalition talks may end in another vote.

headlines.title: Wildfire smoke killed about 3,560 people in Indonesia in September
headlines.summary: A new study estimates that pollution from months of wildfires in Indonesia caused 3,560 deaths in September. The same month, about 57.8 million people in Indonesia were breathing unhealthy to hazardous air.

headlines.title: Court rejects Erin Patterson's appeal against mushroom murder convictions
headlines.summary: Victoria's court of appeal rejected Erin Patterson's bid to overturn her convictions over a beef Wellington lunch that killed three people. The court also ruled that she should be jailed for life with no parole.

headlines.title: Russian drone strike on Dnipro train station kills at least 14
headlines.summary: A Russian drone attack on a train station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed at least 14 people, officials said. At least 14 others were wounded, including an 11-year-old boy.

headlines.title: Brent crude stays over 60% above pre-war levels
headlines.summary: Brent crude is up more than 60 percent compared with pre-war levels, even though oil supply has rebounded. Oil prices eased as the United States sought to revive diplomacy with Iran, though supply risks and possible renewed military escalation limited the losses.

headlines.title: Christine Lagarde to step down from ECB nine months early
headlines.summary: The European Central Bank president will resign nine months ahead of the end of her eight-year term, to have more freedom to speak on matters that are not monetary policy. European Council President Antonio Costa said the process to find a successor is underway.
